positions.landingPage: Send your audience to your website. You can enter the exact page link (destination page) later when creating the ad.
positions.instantForm: Opens a form inside TikTok, so people never leave the app. Usually the cheapest leads, but lead quality is lower than a landing page.
positions.tiktokMessage: Starts a TikTok direct-message thread with your account. Someone has to answer it — replies stall if no one is monitoring the inbox.
positions.instantMessagingApp: Hands the conversation to an external messaging app such as WhatsApp or Messenger. That app account must already be connected to this ad account.
positions.phoneCall: The ad dials a number you provide. Best when a live person can pick up during the hours your ad runs.

help.modeAuto: The system delivers into every available placement and shifts the mix as it learns. The safer choice while an ad group is still learning.

help.tiktok: In-feed and search inventory on TikTok itself — the placement closest to the organic feed.
help.globalAppBundle: Reaches audiences inside other ByteDance apps, beyond TikTok.
help.pangle: TikTok for Business's network on non-TikTok apps and sites: cheaper reach, further from the TikTok feed.
help.allowNaturalComments: Lets organic comments appear under the ad. Extra social proof, and comments you have to moderate.
help.allowComments: Lets viewers comment on the ad. Turning it off keeps the ad quiet but drops that engagement signal.
help.allowDownload: Lets viewers save the video. Wider spread, less control over where the file ends up.
help.allowSharing: Lets viewers share the ad. Adds free reach when the creative works.
help.pangleBlockList: Keeps your ads off the Pangle apps you have block-listed, at the cost of some overall reach.

help.bidStrategy: How TikTok bids for you: chase volume, or hold an average cost. It can be changed later, but it restarts learning.
help.lowestCost: Spends the budget on as many results as it can find, with no bid to maintain. Best while you are still learning what a result costs.
help.maximumVolume: Gets as many results as possible within your budget, without a bid to maintain.
help.costCap: Holds the average cost near the bid you enter. Protects a CPA target, and delivers less when the bid is too low for the auction.
help.budget: This ad group's own budget, daily or lifetime. It appears only when the campaign is not holding one budget for everything.
help.increaseBudgetByGoal: Lets TikTok raise the daily budget on its own while performance keeps meeting your CPA and budget conditions.
help.schedule: Set the time zone first — every start and end time on this card is read in it.
help.continuous: Starts at the time you set and keeps running until you stop it.
help.fixed: Closes the ad group at a fixed moment, which is what a fixed-spend test needs.

help.title: Optional, but without it you only see TikTok-side numbers. Connecting a source lets TikTok attribute sales and optimise toward them.
help.tiktokEventTracking: TikTok's own pixel or events API. This is what reports conversions back, so set it up before you rely on cost-per-conversion figures.
help.thirdPartyIntegration: Third-party measurement URLs fired alongside the ad. Use it when an agency or verification vendor needs its own count.
help.website: The pixel and optimisation event for your site. The event you pick here must be the one the pixel actually fires.
help.applicationEvent: Select the app used for TikTok app event tracking. Leave it empty to disable app event tracking.
help.app: Tracks installs and in-app events for a mobile app. The app must be registered in TikTok Events Manager first.
help.noApp: No app is linked to this ad account yet. Register one in TikTok Events Manager, then it becomes selectable here.
help.crmId: Links this ad to a CRM so offline outcomes can be matched back to the click. Needed if the sale closes outside TikTok.
help.offlineEvent: An event set you upload from outside TikTok — store visits, phone sales. Use it to credit conversions the pixel cannot see.
help.impressionUrl: Fired each time the ad is shown. Must be an HTTPS tracking URL from your measurement vendor, not a landing page.
help.clickUrl: Fired when someone taps the ad. Keep it separate from the destination URL — this one only records the click.
